subject: Acme pilot credits — burn rate check & extension request
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme pilot credits — post-call recap + next steps

Thanks again for your time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Recap:
- Pilot scope: in-app summarization + support ticket triage (two endpoints).
- Observed burn so far (last 10 days): 8.4M generation tokens (attached usage CSV).
- Current average per-request generation: ~800 tokens, ~10k requests/day peaked yesterday (~8.0M tokens/day peak was a short spike, avg ~840k tokens/day over the last week).
- Key ask: you asked about an additional credits extension to complete the remainder of the pilot and validate scaling projections.

Acme asks we cover: ~30 days to finish expanded test, target coverage for expected peak so you can validate SLA. You mentioned a pilot budget range of $10k–$20k if the outcome metrics look good.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I can request a credits extension of $10k to cover the next 30 days of testing (see quick math below).
2) If you want larger scale validation, we can propose a $20k extension and a short committed trial that lowers unit $/1M to a promotional rate.
3) Please confirm which option you prefer and whether you want us to include more aggressive rate-limiting during spikes.

Rough unit economics we discussed on the call (for transparency):
- Standard generation list: $100 / 1M tokens (generation traffic only).
- At that rate, $10k credits ≈ 100M tokens; $20k ≈ 200M tokens.
- Your recent 10-day burn of 8.4M suggests ~25M tokens/month at current activity; our projection for the expanded test (higher concurrency) is ~75M tokens/month.

Recommendation: approve a $10k extension to get through the validation window, with a follow-up review after 2 weeks to inspect real burn vs projection.

Attachments: acme_pilot_usage_20270630.csv (usage by endpoint, per-day); credits_extension_request.docx (customer-facing extension note).

Thanks — I'll wait for the option you’d like (10k or 20k) and will loop in finance for quick approval.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
\

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme pilot credits — post-call recap + next steps

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 8.4M in the 10-day window matches our internal logs (we saw the same spike on Wed as a bot job).
- We’re comfortable with a $10k extension to finish the validation, but we want to make sure that covers the expected peak days (we can stagger load tests over the next 2 weeks).
- Two asks: can you confirm the nominal $/1M for generation (I hear $100 from your note) and whether you’d be willing to provide a short promo rate for the pilot (we’re primarily evaluating unit economics for a potential dedicated capacity purchase).

If we get the extension and a clear $/1M target, we’ll finalize budget internally today and confirm.

Thanks — will hold off on the load tests until you confirm.

Best,
John
Head of Product Engineering | Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com | +1 (617) 555-9987
\

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme pilot credits — post-call recap + next steps — request for credit extension approval

Forwarding the thread — Acme is asking for a $10k extension to complete a 30-day validation. Key datapoints and ask below.

Key datapoints (from customer and our usage):
- 10-day burn: 8.4M generation tokens (attached CSV).
- Daily avg (last 7 days): ~840k gen tokens/day.
- Projected expanded test: ~75M gen tokens/month (this includes planned load tests and increased daily traffic).

Current pricing / impact:
- Standard hosted generation rate: $100 / 1M tokens.
- At that rate, $10k ≈ 100M tokens — should cover the projected month and give headroom for spikes.
- If we offer a promotional pilot unit of $75 / 1M for this extension, $10k buys ~133M tokens and is a stronger goodwill gesture (competitive win).

Recommended ask for approvals:
- Approve $10k credit extension to Acme (applies only to generation tokens for the pilot), with a 30-day window and a usage cap alert at 80% so we can pause if unexpected spikes occur.
- Optionally offer promotional unit econ of $75 / 1M (time-limited for the pilot only).

Operational notes:
- If approved, I’ll send a short DocuSign addendum (credits + window) and update HubSpot (deal ID ACME-2027-045).
- Attachments: acme_pilot_usage_20270630.csv; credits_extension_request.docx (customer-facing wording).

Thoughts? If you’re OK, I’ll request finance to provision the credits and send the DocuSign link to John.

—
Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme pilot credits — post-call recap + next steps — request for credit extension approval

Thanks Marissa — good summary and numbers. Approved.

Approval details:
- Approve $10,000 in pilot credits to Acme Corp, generation-only, valid for 30 days from date of addendum signing.
- Approve promotional pilot unit econ: $75 / 1M tokens for the duration of the pilot (pilot-only, non-recurring).
- Please add an 80% usage alert and a hard cap at 120% of the approved credits (finance should be notified if we hit 100%).

Ops: Marissa — please send the DocuSign addendum (use the template in the shared drive), upload the signed PDF to the HubSpot deal (link below), and mark the deal stage as 'Pilot — Credits Approved'. Finance will provision credits once DocuSign completes.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890
DocuSign link to send: https://docusign.example/ACME-EXT-2027

Thanks — Rachel
